name: Beaujolais

limits: Gamay de Bouze and Gamay de Chaudenay together: at most 10%
rules.yield_base: 68 hl/ha for white, 60 for rosé and red

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

keyfacts: Red Beaujolais is made from Gamay, often by semi-carbonic maceration, with whole clusters fermenting in cement or stainless steel tanks, which gives a fruity wine without much tannin.
There are three tiers: Beaujolais AOC, Beaujolais-Villages AOC covering 39 communes in the north, and Cru Beaujolais with ten villages or areas.
From north to south the ten crus are Saint-Amour, Juliénas, Chénas, Moulin-à-Vent, Fleurie, Chiroubles, Morgon, Régnié, Brouilly and Côte de Brouilly.

blurb.text: A French appellation in the Burgundy region, best known for light-bodied red wine from Gamay, a thin-skinned, low-tannin grape. White is about 1 percent of production, mostly Chardonnay. Crus within it include Morgon, Fleurie, Moulin-à-Vent and Brouilly.
